title: Show thousands separators in displayed amounts + Customers can register twice with different capitalisation
prompt:
Two related tickets in customer accounts and money formatting are being delivered together as one change. Implement all of them in this working tree.

### Ticket 1: Show thousands separators in displayed amounts

Large amounts are hard to read in emails and invoices ("$1234567.89"). Format money with a comma between groups of thousands: `$1,234,567.89`, `-$1,234.50`, `€12,000.00`. Amounts below 1,000 look exactly as they do today.

### Ticket 2: Customers can register twice with different capitalisation

"Ada@Example.com" and "ada@example.com" are treated as two different customers, so one person can end up with two accounts, and a customer who signed up as "Ada@Example.com" cannot log in by typing their address in lower case.

Treat email addresses case-insensitively: store them lower-cased, and look them up regardless of case (whitespace around an address is still ignored). Registering an address that exists in another capitalisation must fail with the usual 409.

couplings.note: t005 x t031: money-grouping changes formatMoney to print $1,000.00; invoice-text's test asserts amounts printed as $1000.00. Merges cleanly, the text invoice test then fails.
t027 x t020: Both change the first lines of registerUser() in users/service.ts: one modifies the email normalisation line, the other adds password checks right after it.
